records.source: שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥דיְהוָ֤ה׀לֹא־גָבַ֣הּ לִ֭בִּי וְלֹא־רָמ֣וּ עֵינַ֑י וְלֹֽא־הִלַּ֓כְתִּי׀בִּגְדֹל֖וֹת וּבְנִפְלָא֣וֹת מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: The song of the ascents, of David. YHWH, not has been haughty my heart, and not have been lifted up my eyes, and not have I walked in great [things] and in [things too] wonderful for me.
pieces: A song of ascents. Of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, there is no pride in my heart, no arrogance in my eyes. I do not go after things too great for me, or too wonderful for me to grasp.

L.1: A song of ascents. Of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my heart has not been lofty, and my eyes have not been raised high; and I have not walked in great things, nor in things too wonderful for me.

R.1: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. By David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I am not proud. I do not look down on others. I do not try to deal with things that are too big or too hard for me to understand.

decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

Four of the Songs of Ascents (122, 124, 131, 133) add "of David", and one (127) "of Solomon". As elsewhere in the Psalms, "of" may mean the psalm is by him, belongs to a collection named for him, or is written for or about him. Some ancient copies of these titles lack the name.

decisions.choice: a high heart, raised eyes: pride
decisions.reason: A heart that is high and eyes that are raised are pictures of pride and of looking down on others (18:28; 101:5; Proverbs 6:17).

decisions.choice: great and wonderful things: what is beyond me
decisions.reason: "Wonderful" (nifla'ot) is used of what is beyond human power or understanding, usually the works of God (Job 42:3). The psalmist does not reach for what belongs to God alone.
To walk in something is to be occupied with it.

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
I am not proud. I do not look down on others.
alternatives: my heart is not lofty; my eyes are not raised
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the two pictures (m4).

records.heading: Calm like a weaned child

records.source: אִם־לֹ֤א שִׁוִּ֨יתִי׀וְדוֹמַ֗מְתִּי נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י כְּ֭גָמֻל עֲלֵ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ כַּגָּמֻ֖ל עָלַ֣י נַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: Surely I have made still and quieted my soul, like a weaned [child] on his mother; like the weaned [child] on me [is] my soul.
pieces: Instead, I have made myself calm and quiet, like a child past nursing age resting on its mother; I am calm within, like that child.

L.2: Surely I have made still and quieted my soul, like a weaned [child] upon its mother; like the weaned [child] upon me [is] my soul.

R.2: Instead, I have made myself calm and peaceful. I am like a young child who no longer needs to nurse and is happy just to rest in its mother's arms. I am at peace like that child.

decisions.choice: if not: surely, on the contrary
decisions.reason: "If not" ('im lo') is the form of an oath, meaning "surely". After the denials of verse 1 it brings the opposite: what the psalmist has done instead.

decisions.choice: a weaned child: content without demanding
decisions.reason: Children were weaned late, at two or three years old (1 Samuel 1:22-24). A weaned child no longer cries to be fed but rests quietly against its mother. So the psalmist rests in the LORD without demanding.

decisions.choice: upon me my soul: my soul within me
decisions.reason: The phrase speaks of the inner self as resting on the person, as the child rests on its mother: "my soul within me" (42:6).
As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

decisions.choice: who no longer needs to nurse and is happy just to rest
decisions.reason: Readable explains what weaned means and why the picture fits (m2).

records.gloss: Hope, Israel, to YHWH from now and until forever.
pieces: Israel, wait in hope for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, from now on and forever.

L.3: Hope, Israel, in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from now and until forever.

R.3: Israel, hope in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, now and forever!

decisions.reason: The same call ends the previous psalm (130:7). The psalmist's quiet trust becomes an example for the whole people.
